title: Thirty Goals Scored, Two Conceded. India's U-18 Hockey Teams Are Dismantling the Asia Cup.
excerpt: The women beat Singapore 25-0. The men hammered Chinese Taipei 13-1. Both teams are in the semifinals in Kakamigahara, Japan.
body:
Thirty goals scored. Two goals conceded. The Indian women's under-18 hockey team has been devastating at the U-18 Asia Cup in Kakamigahara, Japan. And the men's team is not far behind: a 13-1 demolition of Chinese Taipei sealed their semifinal berth after finishing the pool stage with nine points from four matches.

Both Indian teams will play their semifinals on June 5 — the women against China, the men against whichever opponent emerges from Pool B — carrying the kind of scorelines that suggest they came not just to compete, but to overwhelm.

## The Women's Campaign

India's U-18 women topped Pool A with an undefeated record after three commanding wins. They opened with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Malaysia, then beat South Korea 3-1, and then produced a result that borders on the surreal: a 25-0 rout of Singapore in their final pool match.

Ten different players scored in that match alone. Nousheen Naz was the most prolific, netting seven goals to take her tournament tally to 10. Geethasri Nammi, named Player of the Match, scored five. Captain Sweety Kujur added four. Priyanka Minz completed a hat-trick. The depth of scoring, from 10 different names on one scoresheet, speaks to a team that is attacking from everywhere.

India scored in the 2nd minute and never relented. By half-time, it was already beyond doubt. By the final whistle, it was historic.

## The Men's March

The men's U-18 team matched the women's intensity, if not their margin. Against Chinese Taipei, they scored 13 and conceded just one — a consolation penalty corner before half-time.

Ashish Tani Purti starred with a hat-trick, scoring in the 27th, 35th, and 42nd minutes. Gazee Khan, Siddharth Ben, and Rahul Yadav each struck twice. Captain Ketan Kushwaha, Karan Gautam, Premchand Soy, and Varinder Singh also found the net. The goals came from field play and penalty corners alike, a sign of tactical versatility that bodes well for the knockout stage.

India's only blemish in the pool came against hosts Japan, a defeat that denied them a perfect record but did nothing to dent their semifinal credentials.

## What It Means for Indian Hockey

These U-18 results arrive at a time when Indian hockey is trying to build sustained depth beyond its senior teams. The senior men reached the podium at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, the Commonwealth Games in 2022, and the Asian Games in 2023. The women's team has been on a similar upward curve. But the pipeline — the conveyor belt that turns age-group dominance into senior success — is what separates one-off achievements from dynasties.

What Kakamigahara is showing is that the pipeline is healthy. When 10 different players can score in a single match, when a captain's hat-trick is just one of four multi-goal performances, the talent base is wide, not narrow.

## The Diaspora Connection

For Indian hockey fans abroad, these tournaments rarely get live coverage. But the scores travel. A 25-0 scoreline is impossible to scroll past. And the names — Nousheen Naz, Sweety Kujur, Ashish Tani Purti — are the names that will surface again in Asian Games and World Cup squads within two to three years.

India's semifinals are on Thursday. The women face China. The men await their Pool B opponent. If the pool stage is any guide, the opposition should be worried.
